scenario: I volunteer at a winter emergency shelter that becomes overcrowded whenever temperatures drop, and because beds are limited, the shelter prioritizes people with serious medical or physical vulnerabilities. On one especially busy night, I was helping sort intake forms while staff tried to place the last available beds. The temperature outside is chilly, so anyone who is unable to be placed with a bed will face discomfort outside. A man approached my coworker and pointed out several severe medical conditions he had listed, which would move him to the top of the priority list. Later, I overheard him telling a friend that he had lied about those conditions to nab a spot inside. There are still a handful of people waiting to have their intake forms processed. If I secretly move the man's intake form to the bottom of the priority list, his bed will go to someone else. If I do not do this, another person will be turned away and left to experience discomfort.
entities: I,1 coworker the man approached about his intake form,1 man who lied about severe medical conditions to get a bed,1 friend the man later told about the lie,a handful minus 1 other people still waiting to have their intake forms processed,the other shelter staff handling intake and bed placement
outcomes: The man keeps his high priority status for a shelter bed
The man receives one of the last available beds
Another person is not given that bed
That person remains outside in the cold
Shelter staff place someone based on false medical information
